This invitation expired. Remove it and create another.
Sync stops on this phone now and on %1$s when it reconnects. Files stay on both devices. Sharing again requires a new invitation.

Stop storing backups on this phone?
This phone stops holding copies for your other devices, and its storage service shuts down. Copies already here stay encrypted, but no new copy can arrive until you turn this back on.
The pairing files saved on this phone are deleted. Nothing was trusted, and you would have to start pairing again from the beginning.
The pairing request with “%1$s” ends now. Neither device is given access, and you would have to start again.
Importing this file removes %1$s from the remembered list on your Covalent server. Backed-up data already stored is not deleted, but this list cannot be rebuilt without another settings file.

Enter the secure web address your Covalent server shows. Android asks for local network access before the first check.

On the computer where your Covalent server was set up, run covalent claim. Then, on this phone, enter the server’s exact HTTPS address, choose the local-api-token file it created, and add root.crt below. This phone never accepts a setup code.
Setup URL opened. Check the address, then enter your access token.
That setup URL was ignored because this app is already connected. To use a different Covalent server, open Settings and choose Change server connection.
That setup URL did not contain a usable server address, so nothing was changed.
Choose local-api-token created by covalent claim, or paste its exact contents above.
Your access token is only ever sent over an encrypted connection. An unencrypted address is accepted only when the server runs on this phone.
A publicly trusted address needs no extra setup. For a private Covalent certificate, add exactly one certificate file or one certificate fingerprint. Android still checks that the address matches.
Or use an exact certificate fingerprint
The fingerprint must match a certificate the server presents. Covalent never skips this check.

For a packaged Covalent server, use the root.crt and access token created by covalent claim on your trusted computer. Transfer root.crt to this phone over a trusted direct channel, and use the exact web address you claimed.
Android needs local network permission before Covalent can reach an address on your own network.
Local network access was not granted, so Covalent did not contact that address.
Folder access saved. Covalent will tell you if Android later takes it away.
Use a complete web address without a username or password in it.
A server on another machine must use an encrypted https address. An unencrypted address works only when the server runs on this phone.
Enter your Covalent server’s access token.
That token file is not a valid local-api-token claim output.
Enter a 64-character hexadecimal fingerprint, or one in sha256/base64 form.
That Covalent server could not be verified.

Open Covalent on both devices. Find the other device below or enter its address, then compare the confirmation code on both screens before either gets access.
No device on your network answered. Check local network permission, or enter the other device’s Tailscale address below.

Tailscale cannot list your devices for Covalent. Enter the other device’s Tailscale name or IP address once.
Automatic discovery on your network is off. Enter the address the other device shows. Both devices still confirm the same code.

Use this only when the two devices cannot reach each other over the network. You carry three small files between them: a pairing file, a reply file, then a final file. Choose which device this phone is, then follow the steps in order.
Compare this confirmation code with the one on the other device. Confirm on both only if every group matches. Pairing copies nothing now; you choose this device separately when creating a backup.
Confirmed here. Now confirm the same code on the other device.
Device added for backups, with its signed certificate fingerprint.
Saving the signed connection to this device…
Secure pairing failed. Nothing was trusted.
The signed pairing already carries the other device’s address and certificate fingerprint. Nothing else to enter.
This older pairing has no signed connection details. Start a new direct pairing — Covalent never accepts an address or certificate typed in by hand.
Reply file from the other device
The other device has not confirmed yet. Confirm there first, then open its new reply file here.
Send this final file to the other device and open it there with “Open final file”. Then choose Finish pairing on this phone.

resources.string: Choose the folder again to restore this link. Covalent keeps the previous folder choice until this phone confirms the replacement.
Covalent saved your folder choice. Retry the repair to finish restoring this link.
Licenses and notices for the open source software included with Covalent.
Covalent could not verify the notices included in this app.
New versions of Covalent are published on GitHub. Download the new APK there and install it over this one. Covalent does not check for updates by itself.
Pair a device, choose a source folder and a recipient, then choose when files transfer. Files go one way only, from the source to the recipient.

1. Open Covalent on the other device. It can be a Mac, a server or another phone.
2. On this phone, find it under nearby devices or enter its device address, then choose Pair device.
3. Compare the confirmation code on both screens. If the codes match, confirm on both.

Pairing copies nothing.
Compare this confirmation code with the one on the other device. Confirm on both only if every group matches. Pairing copies nothing now; you choose a folder separately after pairing.
Enter the device’s new numeric IP address and port. Covalent will verify the same trusted device before saving it.

If this failed after an interrupted copy, choose Settings, enable Restore files deleted at the destination, and confirm before the next run. Files you deleted at a destination may download again.
If a deleted source file may still have an unknown copy at a destination, restore the source file or remove only that copy before retrying.
This link uses shared Android Wi-Fi or charging requirements. Change them in shared settings on any linked device.
One-way sync. Originals stay on this phone. Deleting a received copy will not copy it back.
